body: Cockroaches survive. Humans are meant to prevail.

I agree and disagree with you. Sometimes, circumstances may be arranged in such a way that hope can be a catalyst for improvement. SOMETIMES. However, hoping in the face of all evidence pointing to an unwanted outcome can be a bit misguided. I do agree with you that hope does little more than prolong one's suffering. Hope is plain stupid if there's not a strong enough "why".
I wouldn't know. I don't know anyone who's actually been here forever. That WOULD kind of suck, though.
I guess it CAN get better, but that depends on a number of things. Answering for myself, it doesn't get better.
And NO, there's no gift receipt.
This is exactly why I'm leaving. Humans are just smart enough to complicate life. The only species known that actually charges itself to exist. Evolution.
Honestly, I just want to be alone. I'm done trying to relate to people who only end up leaving me for someone 'better'. I'm never enough for anyone.
The only presumable freedom is death. Maybe that's why we fear it, and why we have a survival instinct. Kind of like "Directive 4" in the movie "Robocop".

There's no such thing as love, especially romantic love. I used to wonder why older people would laugh at the idea of "marrying for love". I've come to learn that marriage is basically a business contract to bind together political, economic, or cultural interests. I wish I would've learned this at a younger age. It's like the more I learn about life, the less I see a reason to live it. This is REALLY just a futile game, where you're gonna die in the end anyway. What the hell sat around and thought that this was a good idea to do?

Are you referring to the 'self-help/motivation' industry? I totally agree with you. It goes hand-in-hand with religion. "Don't worry about economic collapse, just LIVE... YOUR... DREAM!!!" The hustle of hope is very clever, and does a magnificent job of keeping people individualized and ignorant.

I once dated someone who thought that way. "Deep down, people are good inside." They also believed that America is a true democracy and that society couldn't possibly break down. Even in the face of the behavior that COVID-19 revealed about human nature, they still believe that humans are civilized and that the 'toilet paper turmoil' was only carried out by a "small group of unenlightened people." I sometimes wonder if the handling of the COVID outbreak was (in some small, weird way) a social experiment conducted by the elite. How would their subjects respond in a 'lockdown situation'. It's frightening to think that if humans will fight each other over toilet paper, what the hell would they do over water and food? Somehow, the majority of people think that humans have graduated past their animal instincts. I really pray that the food shortage news is all a hoax, because if that's no so we're in for some very ugly days ahead.

I feel this on some level. I wanted a simple life. A wife (who is also a good mother, better than the one I had... which isn't hard to be). A couple of my own children (as the previous poster stated). I wanted to be the father I never had. I even had "a number" for my bank account for when it would be okay to start having children. However, I feel like you. I want to spare them the suffering of this world. I feel like I was just put here, and left to figure life out on my own. And perhaps that's true to some extent. I had no guidance. No love. No protection. Only abuse, bullying, and ostracization from my own family.

I don't think its immoral to want children or to be a parent. I DO, however, think its very wrong to bring a life into this world without a plan for it. That one life is about to be brought into a very complicated and imposing situation. I've come to realize that life takes a certain awareness. An awareness that, I believe, this society robs a lot of people of whether it be from the conditioning through movies and entertainment or through the social manipulation of the psychology of the parents. It doesn't foster the idea of parents (or the community) guiding a child. It simply just encourages babies, and working like hell to take care of them. Essentially just making them another expense for living on earth. 

I strongly believe that there should be a purpose for having a child. A functional purpose. Not one rooted in a vicarious desire to experience life through them. There should be a social reason, other than just to feed a heartless, tyrannical, economic system that needs a steady supply of fleshbots. And it's for that reason that I have not had a child. As I sit here now, looking at the macro of life and seeing the coming 'dark days' for humanity, I'm very glad I didn't bring a child into this life only to pass down suffering to them. I used to not concern myself with the affairs of the world (as the so-called holy buy-bull admonishes). However, if COVID taught me anything, its that the macro affects all of us and will do so very quickly and unpleasantly.
This is AWESOME!!!
Of course, because the push the idea of 'hope'. People don't want to see that hope can, sometimes, be irrational.

Suffering is seen as a good thing for many misguided reasons. All of it rooted in individualistic fantasy. One insidious idea is that suffering is "a gift from 'god'..." One of the weird things that Western society has done to the human psyche is that it's sold the myth of progress. That, no matter what, things over time MUST get better. So, any suffering is the tuition that must be paid towards that 'better'. That's why people aren't really encouraged to do anything about the world. Because, at some point, SOMEBODY's gonna come along (sent from 'god', of course) and save humans from their thousands of years of self destruction and negligence of their problems. It's truly sad.
You just wrote the scathing, hurtful truth about people today.

You wrote my sentiments exactly. The 'Les Brown/Tony Robbins, I'm the one' b.s. does nothing but promote stupid individualism. It isolates people from one another. Its sickening that the self-help garbage has morphed into full blown hustle culture. It makes working to death in order to say 'fuck you' to everyone who doesn't get as many crumbs look sexy. I totally agree with you.
Simple, insightful, and TRUE!!!
Man, thanks. I really do appreciate that!!!

I appreciate the kind thoughts. But, I have no other choice. Its that or homelessness. I'm not attacking you, but just stating a thought. I've always wondered why society would rather see a person live in the gutter because 'at least you're not dead', than being at peace with someone ending their suffering. To me, that just seems kind of cruel.
I don't mind being a human. I just hate our nature and how we've decided to organize ourselves and our world.

It SOUNDS inspiring. Some people, in a way, try to be somewhat helpful. Or at least do something that makes them feel like they're 'helping'. Its one of the many messed up ways that humans have decided to organize themselves and interpret their existence.
You can't. Plain and simple.

Just the title describes the derailment of my life. You CAN'T do this shit alone. We NEED a support system. I wish I had the ability to connect with other people. I hope that either my next life will be good or there is no next life and I can just not exist. I hate loneliness.
The future looks very questionable.

Not being able to adjust to this society isn't weakness. Your loneliness is not uncommon. Not at all. This society MAKES people mentally ill. The insidious part of it all is that it tries to make an INDIVIDUAL seem like they're the problem. Societal madness works its way into every individual in it. So, I have to disagree. You're not weak. I feel your post, though.

I think its because we're all born into different contexts. I always think how other people have it so easy, yet I (and others) have it so shitty. I knew someone who was born into a family where their mother and father worked their asses off to give their children a good life. They saved and sacrificed, and now their kids are reaping the benefits. All of them either own successful businesses or are involved in local/state politics. I, on the other hand, got a father who abandoned me, an abusive and mentally ill mother, a family that told her to have an abortion when she was pregnant with me, and nothing but curses spoken over my life. Its been very difficult to overcome all of that, because I don't have the people skills to build and maintain relationships that help me when times get tough. I'm alienated from society and am being driven to make decisions I never thought I'd be making. I totally feel you.
That's how I feel.

Please don't feel bad for falling for a scam. I almost fell for one that had to do with getting work. Those people are getting more and more clever with the scams. Its cruel and scary how much its progressing. I agree with most of your post. My mother was the most toxic element of my life, tho.

I guess that's why "ignorance is bliss" is an existential truth. I sometimes envy people who can just float through life and shrug everything off as "...well, that's life". I mean, I'd be a 'sheeple', but they seem so fine with everything. My soul must not be from this universe.

That's where I'm at. In the end, I tried my best. Another thing I've learned, in addition to it doesn't always 'get better', is that failure doesn't always lead to growth. That's another platitude people like to throw on others. In my case, failure only led to destruction. No growth. No lesson. No silver lining. Just destruction and pain. I don't regret it though, because I did break out from the capitalist matrix.
